whatWasMissing.note: The model has been able to switch cylinders since the migration began — InputIntent carries switchGasIndex and applyGasSwitchIntent implements the rules, with unit coverage in tests/unit/dive-model.test.ts. Nothing in the client ever set the field, so a two-cylinder dive could be configured on the setup screen and then stayed on the first cylinder for the whole dive.
whatWasMissing.consequence: #158 shipped multi-cylinder configuration whose only effect in the dive was the starting gas.

boundsPortedFromTheOracle.keyBindings: src/game-loop.js TASK-019 — `for (var i = 0; i < tankCount; i++)` over String(i + 1), so 1 to 6 and no further; MAX_TANKS is 6
boundsPortedFromTheOracle.refusalRules: src/game-loop.js `i !== activeTank && tanks[i].gasRemaining > 0`, which src/core/dive-model.ts applyGasSwitchIntent already implements, plus its own refusal of any switch while ccr is set
boundsPortedFromTheOracle.rowVisibility: src/ui.js and src/touch.js show cylinder slots only where the mode has more than one cylinder

deliberateDesign.queuedNotImmediate: The model moves in whole-second steps and `advance` with elapsedS 0 returns the state untouched, so the switch lands on the next step — up to a second later, where legacy applies it within the frame. That is the fixed-step design of this client rather than anything about gas switching: every intent it has, the ascent keys included, is sampled the same way. A press between steps is kept rather than dropped, which is what the request being cleared after a step consumes it (not when it is read) buys, and there is an e2e test for it.
deliberateDesign.rulesStayInTheModel: The controller decides nothing about whether a switch is allowed. It passes an index; src/core/dive-model.ts refuses the active cylinder, an empty one and CCR. Duplicating those checks in the UI would have created a second place for them to drift.
deliberateDesign.emptyCylinderStaysVisible: Disabled rather than removed, and it keeps its contrast instead of fading to the usual grey. An empty cylinder is not a broken control, and a cylinder that vanishes mid-dive is worse than one that says why it cannot be chosen.
deliberateDesign.delegatedClickHandler: The buttons do not exist when the dive starts — the first frame builds them from the state — so the click listener sits on the container. A listener per button would have to be rebound on every rebuild.
deliberateDesign.buttonsBuiltOnce: syncTankControls creates the buttons only when the count changes and thereafter updates attributes. Rebuilding them each frame would discard focus sixty times a second, and unlike the setup screen there is no re-render to restore it from.

sliceBoundary.deviation: Gas info is its own PR. It is five rendered pages with their own cycling rules — src/state.js infoPageMode 0-5, skipping the tanks page below four cylinders, toggling 0<->5 in CCR, and unavailable in rec entirely — which is larger than the switch and unrelated to it. The slicing in an issue is a hint, not a contract.
sliceBoundary.stillOutstandingInThisIssue: gas info (I), fast-forward (F), torch as a first-class intent, CCR setpoint ([ ]) and bailout (B), and the HUD additions the issue lists: active cylinder, loop PO2 vs setpoint, scrubber time, bailout state, fast-forward indicator.

notTestedAndWhy.requestClearedAfterAStep: Clearing the queued request once a step consumes it is correct intent semantics, but it has no observable consequence today: the model treats a repeat of the active index as a no-op, so a request left set produces no extra gas-switch event and no visible difference. A test would have passed with the clearing removed. Recorded here instead of written, on the rule that a test which cannot fail proves nothing.
notTestedAndWhy.gasSwitchNotification: Legacy shows a two-second 'GAS SWITCH -> T{n}' toast and resets bestGasAlerted and fastForwardActive. The toast belongs with the HUD additions and fastForwardActive with the fast-forward slice; neither exists yet, so neither is reproduced.
notTestedAndWhy.noUnitTests: The behaviour added here is the controller's queue and the DOM sync, and both need a running animation frame. The node test environment has no requestAnimationFrame — tests/unit already notes this for destroy() — so the coverage is e2e, where the real loop runs, rather than a mock that would assert the mock.

counterCheck.method: One revert at a time, with the build result read before each run.

cases.intentWiring: the queued index never reaches the intent — the digit, button and between-steps tests all fail

cases.rowVisibility: the row no longer hides itself — the CCR test fails

counterCheck.oneRevertHadToBeFixedFirst: Setting the intent to a bare null left #requestedTankIndex written but never read, which TS6133 rejects; the build failed and the run that followed would have been against a stale dist/. The script reported the failed build and skipped the result rather than reporting a pass. The revert was rewritten to keep reading the field so the comparison is about behaviour and not about whether it compiles.

releaseLabel.reasoning: Deployed bytes change — deploy.yml runs `pages deploy src/` with no ignore file — but served behaviour does not: _redirects sends / to the legacy client and the migration client stays unreachable until the #170 cutover.
releaseLabel.note: The owner resolved this for #179 by setting release:none by hand over the bot's release:minor, which the feat prefix produces. The same reasoning applies here, and the same manual step will be needed.

durableProvenance.why: measuredCommit is a branch commit, and every PR here is squash-merged with the branch deleted, so it becomes unreachable from main the moment this lands. Checked across the repository: all six evidence artifacts record a measuredCommit that origin/main cannot reach, so the usual `git rev-parse <measuredCommit>^{tree}` recipe is reproducible only for whoever still has the branch. Raised as a P3 on PR #176 for one artifact; it turned out to be structural.
durableProvenance.check: Subtree hashes survive the squash, because the squash commit carries the same content. After this merges, run `git rev-parse <squash-merge-commit>:src <squash-merge-commit>:tests <squash-merge-commit>:scripts` and compare with the three below. Verified on two already-merged PRs: #179 (115c33f vs 3340d60) and #176 (12b567e vs 00c709c), all three subtrees identical in both.
durableProvenance.caveat: This holds because the only commit after the measured one adds this artifact, which touches nothing under src, tests or scripts. If a later commit on the branch changes any of them, these hashes stop matching and the measurement no longer describes what shipped — which is the point of recording them.
